title: In Silicon Valley, AI founders cheer Trump’s calls for the industry to police itself on safety
source_used: Associated Press, read on the Kokomo Tribune copy (opening paragraphs only)
key_facts: At Tech Week in San Francisco, venture capitalists and AI founders are ebullient about the White House's hands-off approach to AI regulation.
President Trump recently hosted tech leaders in Washington and signed a voluntary safety pact for AI.
AP says the pact encourages AI labs to self-monitor but lacks detailed safety measures.
Silicon Valley companies have disclosed their models' involvement in myriad troubling cyberattacks this year, yet the sector keeps driving economic growth.
The Trump administration has reoriented federal policy away from oversight and toward rapid tech growth.
AP says the nation is further from governing AI systems than it was a few years ago, after months of debate about AI agents meddling with government websites and healthcare data.
quote_evidence: SAN FRANCISCO (AP) — Tech Week is in full bloom in San Francisco, packing the city’s restaurants this week with venture capitalists and AI founders ebullient about the White House’s stance on regulating artificial intelligence — namely, don’t do it.

And after months of debate about leading AI companies’ unchecked AI agents meddling with everything from U.S. government websites to healthcare data, the nation now finds itself further from governing AI systems than it was a few years ago.
This agreement encourages AI labs to self-monitor but lacks detailed safety measures.
why_it_matters_hint: Industry backing for voluntary safety rules leaves the public relying on company self-monitoring.
event_date: Week of 5-11 Oct 2026 (Tech Week); the pact was signed 29 Sep 2026
